<h2>The Trial Plan: Free to Start</h2>
<p>Railway’s Trial plan is genuinely free — no credit card required. You get a one-time $5 usage credit to spin up services and see how the platform works. Once your credit runs out, you’ll need to upgrade to keep things running.</p>
<p><strong>What you get on Trial:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>$5 one-time free usage credit</li>
<li>512MB RAM per service</li>
<li>1GB disk per service</li>
<li>Access to all deployment features</li>
<li>Community support</li>
</ul>
<p>The Trial is honestly great for evaluating Railway. You can deploy a real app, connect a database, and get a feel for the developer experience before spending a dime. For most small test apps, $5 of credit will last a few days to a week.</p>
<h2>The Hobby Plan: $5/Month for Indie Developers</h2>
<p>The Hobby plan is <a href="https://thesoftwarescout.com/go/railway/" target="_blank" rel="noopener sponsored">Railway’s</a> entry-level paid tier at <strong>$5/month</strong>. Here’s the key thing to understand: that $5 fee includes $5 of usage credits. So if your app uses exactly $5 of resources per month, you pay nothing beyond the base fee.</p>
<p>If you use more than $5 of resources, you pay the overage at usage rates.</p>
<p><strong>Hobby plan includes:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>$5/month in usage credits included</li>
<li>Up to 8GB RAM per service</li>
<li>Up to 32GB disk per service</li>
<li>Custom domains</li>
<li>Private networking</li>
<li>Priority email support</li>
<li>Unlimited projects</li>
</ul>
<p>For a simple Node.js or Python app with a PostgreSQL database, the Hobby plan often costs right around $5–$8/month total — very reasonable.</p>
<h2>The Pro Plan: $20/Month for Serious Projects</h2>
<p>The Pro plan at <strong>$20/month</strong> targets teams and production workloads. Like Hobby, the base fee includes $20 of usage credit. Beyond that, you pay usage-based rates.</p>
<p><strong>Pro plan adds:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>$20/month in usage credits included</li>
<li>Higher resource limits (up to 32GB RAM per service)</li>
<li>Team collaboration features</li>
<li>Multiple team members</li>
<li>Priority support</li>
<li>Spend limits to prevent bill shock</li>
<li>Metrics and observability</li>
</ul>
<p>The Pro plan is worth it the moment you need team access or your resource usage regularly exceeds what the Hobby plan covers.</p>
<h2>How Railway’s Usage-Based Pricing Actually Works</h2>
<p>This is where <a href="https://thesoftwarescout.com/go/railway/" target="_blank" rel="noopener sponsored">Railway</a> gets interesting — and where a lot of people get confused. Railway charges per actual resource consumption, not for reserved capacity you may or may not use.</p>
<p><strong>Railway’s resource rates (approximate):</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>CPU:</strong> ~$0.000463/vCPU per minute</li>
<li><strong>RAM:</strong> ~$0.000231/GB per minute</li>
<li><strong>Disk:</strong> ~$0.000135/GB per minute</li>
<li><strong>Network egress:</strong> $0.10/GB (after free allowance)</li>
</ul>
<div style="background: #f8fafc; padding: 16px; border-radius: 8px; margin: 20px 0;">
<strong>Real-world example:</strong> A Node.js app using 0.5 vCPU and 512MB RAM 24/7 costs approximately:<br>
CPU: 0.5 x $0.000463 x 43,200 min/month = ~$10/month<br>
RAM: 0.5GB x $0.000231 x 43,200 min/month = ~$5/month<br>
<strong>Total: ~$15/month</strong> — within the Pro plan’s $20 credit.
</div>
<p>The key insight: Railway only charges when your services are actually running. If you sleep or pause services during low-traffic periods, you’re not paying for them. This is fundamentally different from platforms that charge for reserved capacity.</p>

<h2>What’s Included: Key Features by Plan</h2>
<h3>Services & Deployments</h3>
<p>All paid Railway plans include unlimited projects and services. You can deploy as many apps, databases, and background workers as you want — you just pay for their resource consumption. This is a huge advantage over platforms that charge per-service.</p>
<h3>Databases</h3>
<p>Railway natively supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, and Redis deployments. Each database instance counts toward your usage like any other service — you pay for the CPU, memory, and storage consumed. For a small PostgreSQL instance, expect around $1–$3/month on light workloads.</p>
<h3>Networking & Domains</h3>
<p>Custom domains are included on all paid plans. Railway provides automatic HTTPS/SSL certificates at no extra charge. Each service gets a private railway.app subdomain out of the box.</p>
<h3>Spend Controls</h3>
<p>One of Railway’s best features for cost management: <strong>spend limits</strong>. On the Pro plan, you can set a hard monthly spend cap. Once you hit your limit, Railway will stop services rather than letting your bill balloon — crucial for preventing unexpected costs.</p>
<h2>Is Railway Cheap or Expensive?</h2>
<p>The honest answer depends on your workload pattern:</p>

<ul>
<li>Your app has variable or bursty traffic</li>
<li>You run multiple small services</li>
<li>You want to avoid paying for idle capacity</li>
<li>You have side projects with low traffic</li>
<li>You value simplicity over granular control</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div style="background: #fef2f2; padding: 16px; border-radius: 8px;">

<ul>
<li>You need 24/7 high-compute workloads</li>
<li>Your app does heavy data processing</li>
<li>You have high network egress (large file transfers)</li>
<li>You need dedicated CPU instances</li>
<li>You’re on a fixed budget and need predictable costs</li>
</ul>
</div>

<h2>Railway Pricing: Common Real-World Scenarios</h2>
<h3>Scenario 1: Personal Blog or Portfolio API</h3>
<p>A lightweight Node.js API with minimal traffic, running 24/7: <strong>~$2–$5/month</strong>. Easily covered by the Hobby plan’s $5 credit. Effective cost: just the $5/month base fee.</p>
<h3>Scenario 2: Startup MVP with Database</h3>
<p>A Next.js app + PostgreSQL database with moderate traffic: <strong>~$8–$15/month</strong>. Slightly above the Hobby credit threshold — you’d pay $5 base + $3–$10 overage. Still very affordable.</p>
<h3>Scenario 3: Production SaaS Application</h3>
<p>Multiple microservices, a database, Redis cache, background workers: <strong>$25–$60/month</strong>. The Pro plan’s $20 credit helps offset costs, but heavy usage will exceed it. Compare this to Heroku’s dyno model or a comparable AWS/GCP setup — Railway is usually competitive.</p>
<h3>Scenario 4: High-Traffic App</h3>
<p>At scale, with significant CPU and egress costs: Railway can get expensive. A high-traffic app might need $100–$300/month. At that scale, evaluate whether Railway’s convenience premium over raw cloud infrastructure is worth it to your team.</p>
<h2>Tips to Keep Your Railway Bill Low</h2>
<ol>
<li><strong>Use sleep mode for development services</strong> — Railway can put services to sleep when not in use. Enable this for dev/staging environments to avoid paying for idle time.</li>
<li><strong>Set spend limits</strong> — Always configure a monthly spend cap on the Pro plan to avoid surprise bills.</li>
<li><strong>Monitor your resource usage</strong> — Railway’s dashboard shows real-time resource consumption. Keep an eye on memory leaks and CPU spikes.</li>
<li><strong>Use Railway’s cost estimator</strong> — Before deploying, use the official pricing calculator to estimate monthly costs for your expected workload.</li>
<li><strong>Right-size your services</strong> — Don’t allocate 8GB RAM to a service that only needs 512MB.</li>
</ol>

For apps with consistent, predictable load, Render’s fixed pricing can be more predictable. For variable or bursty workloads, Railway often wins on cost.</p>

The usage-based model rewards efficient code and variable traffic patterns. The developer experience is genuinely exceptional — deploys are fast, the dashboard is clean, and the database integration is seamless.</p>

<h2>Frequently Asked Questions</h2>
<h3>Does Railway have a free plan?</h3>
<p>Railway doesn’t have a permanent free tier. Instead, they offer a Trial plan with $5 of one-time usage credit — no credit card needed. Once the credit runs out, you upgrade to Hobby ($5/month) or Pro ($20/month). The trial is enough to properly evaluate the platform before committing.</p>
<h3>Can Railway pricing surprise you with unexpected costs?</h3>
<p>It can, which is why the spend limit feature on Pro is so important. Always set a monthly cap. The usage-based model means a traffic spike or memory leak can drive costs up fast without a limit in place.</p>
<h3>Is Railway cheaper than Heroku?</h3>
<p>Generally yes. Railway’s Hobby plan at $5/month typically delivers more resources than Heroku’s comparable dynos, and Railway’s usage-based model can be significantly cheaper for low-traffic apps that only need resources part of the time.</p>
<h3>What payment methods does Railway accept?</h3>
<p>Railway accepts major credit cards. For Enterprise plans, invoicing arrangements are available. All billing is handled through <a href="https://thesoftwarescout.com/go/railway/" target="_blank" rel="noopener sponsored">Railway’s platform</a> directly.</p>
<h3>Does Railway charge for databases separately?</h3>
<p>No — Railway databases are just services like any other, and you pay for their resource consumption (CPU, memory, disk) at the same usage rates. There’s no separate database pricing tier, which makes Railway particularly economical for apps with multiple database instances.</p>
